As DBH is often used as a proxy of tree height in most tree species, we only considered DBH as measure of tree size, which is an important structural trait, critical in forest ecology and for above ground biomass estimate. Canopy cover was assessed at four continuous 10 m  10 m assessment areas along the transect using a visual cover method (Humphrey et al., 1999). Percentage of vegetation cover on each plot was calculated from 10 random $1 \; \mathrm { { m } } \times 1$ m quadrats along the transect (Rahman et al., 2015). We also measured species richness and average height of herbaceous plant species in three random $5 \mathrm { ~ m ~ } \times 5$ m sampling subplots within each sampling plot. An important environmental factor, the nearest distance from the centre of sampling plot to river bank (the distance to river, Magagula, 2003; Rykken et al., 2007) was measured by using ENVI version 5.4 based on satellite images.
